findings.where: Nav bar 'Destinations' link (desktop inline, phone behind Menu); nav wordmark home link; footer links 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: None of the page's links lead anywhere useful except the email link. 'Destinations' points to #destinations, an anchor that does not exist on this page. The wordmark's home link, Privacy, Terms and Report content all return to this same page. So a visitor who has finished reading and wants to look at Bali or Lombok hostels has no route out, can't reach the home page, and can't read the privacy or terms pages the footer promises.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker. They came to check whether the ranking is fair before choosing somewhere to stay. Their next step is to browse hostels, and the one link that offers that does nothing. Dead legal links on a page about honesty also make the site look unfinished.

findings.where: End of the page, after 'Hostelworld, for comparison', just above the footer
findings.fault: The page ends with a paragraph about a competitor's review window. It never closes on Manta and gives no next step, such as a link to the Bali or Lombok destination guides. The last thing the visitor reads before the footer is about Hostelworld.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who is now convinced but has nowhere obvious to go. The founder would object too: the brief says the positioning never anchors on a competitor, and here the competitor gets the page's final word.

findings.fault: The headings don't match their content. Most of 'Ranking method' explains how a score is built: pulling toward the area average, which reviews count, the reward-code badge, what zero reviews shows. 'Scoring method' holds only the decay rule. The page also never says plainly what orders the results list, for example whether hostels are sorted by score or how vibe and surf distance come in. That leaves the h1's promise, 'how a hostel's position is decided', only half kept.
findings.who_objects: A sceptical visitor who wants to know why hostel A sits above hostel B. They read the ranking section and come away knowing what can't buy a position, but not what actually decides it.

findings.where: Body copy throughout, worst in the 'Ranking method' paragraphs and the single sentence that makes up the 'Hostelworld, for comparison' paragraph
findings.fault: The text is long, dense and full of internal terms a traveller doesn't use: 'partner tier', 'direct booking exit', 'listing presence', 'weighted count of recent reviews', 'the one count where a hostel's listing changes is zero'. Several sentences run past 40 words, and the Hostelworld paragraph is one sentence of about 70. On a phone this becomes a wall more than two screens tall.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker reading on a phone, often mid-trip on a poor connection. They want the gist in seconds and get policy prose written from an operator's point of view, so the trust point stays buried.

findings.where: Whole page at desktop width (1440 px)
findings.fault: One narrow text column hugs the left edge of the container and leaves about 60% of the screen empty sand on the right, under a nav that spans the full width. There is no illustration, colour or brand moment anywhere between the nav and the footer. The page reads like a bare legal document, not a MantaHostels page.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the brand names sterile and corporate as the enemy and wants decorative surfaces led by illustration. The visitor may also take the lopsided, empty layout as an unfinished page, which works against a page meant to build trust.

findings.where: Intro: the lede, the 'Scores weight toward recent stays…' paragraph, the three-point list, and the first sentence of 'Ranking method'
findings.fault: The intro says the same thing three times in a row. The small paragraph is restated by list points 2 and 3, and point 1 comes back word for word as the opening of 'Ranking method'. The three key promises are also set as an ordinary numbered list at body size, which suggests steps or a ranking, not three separate guarantees. Nothing makes them stand out as the summary someone skimming should take away.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the first screen: they read the same claim several times before reaching anything new, and the takeaways look no more important than the body text.

findings.where: Top of the page, near the h1 or the intro
findings.fault: The method is not dated or versioned. There is no 'last updated' line, so a reader can't tell whether this is the rule in force now.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor checking whether the published method is current: a method page with no date is weaker proof, while the competitor claim further down does carry a date.

findings.where: Footer link row at phone width
findings.fault: The row wraps after 'How we rank', leaving a stray '·' separator at the end of the first line with nothing after it.
findings.who_objects: Few visitors would notice, but it looks like a layout slip in the footer on every page at phone width.
